name: math-library
title: Math function reference
summary: Sixteen expression functions evaluated on sample arguments (sqrt, pow, exp, ln, log, hypot, square, atan2, floor, ceil, round, fract, abs, sign, max), each shown with its result.
prompt: Make a reference card of RemoteCompose's math functions: show sqrt(2), pow(2, 10), exp(1), ln(10), log(1000), hypot(3, 4), square(1.5), atan2(1, 1), floor/ceil/round/fract of negative numbers, abs, sign and max, each with its value.
teaches: Call the math functions inside any expression string: sqrt, pow(x, n), exp, ln (natural), log (base 10), hypot(x, y), square, floor, ceil, round, fract, abs, sign, min, max
Check rounding on negative numbers: floor(-2.5) is -3, ceil(-2.5) is -2, fract(-2.25) is -0.25 (x minus its truncation)
Print a computed value with textFromFloat; flags 519 (7 + 512 OPTIONS_ROUNDING) rounds the last decimal instead of cutting it
pitfalls: log is base 10 and ln is natural: log(1000) = 3, ln(10) = 2.303
round is Java's Math.round, half rounds UP: round(-2.5) = -2 (the C++ player gives -3, see the family's findings)
mad(a, b, c) is a * b + c in the reference (and the TS player); the C++ player computes a + b * c, so mad(2, 3, 4) shows 14 instead of 10. Write a * b + c until it is fixed
The JSON parser has no deg(), rad(), cbrt(), log2(), mod() or mix(): they are runtime operators without a JSON name, and an unknown name fails with "Unknown token". Multiply by 57.29578 for degrees

Two fixed 160 dp columns need about 330 dp: in a narrower host the second column is squeezed off. Put the cells in a flow (widthIn max two cells so the columns survive a wider host) and let the page scroll

snippets.note: the sixteen cells in a flow capped at 328 dp (two 164 dp cells a line), so a narrower host gets one column and the page scrolls

check.describe: Sixteen cells: 1.414, 1024, 2.718, 2.303, 3, 5, 2.25, 0.785 on the left; -3, -2, 3, -2, -0.25, 4, -1, 8 on the right. Resized, the cells sit in a flow capped at two 164 dp cells a line: at 234 wide they stack in one column (powers and rounding alternating) and the page scrolls; at 540 the two columns stay together, centred.
